Sunday, 02 April, 2028: The Crown Responds Publicly to the attack

[spoiler=The Article][quote=koranvistan;61479697]▌▌▌[b]V E L N A Z - T I M E S[/b] []---------[] [i]W E D N E S D A Y - 15 - M A R C H , 2028[/i]▐▐▐
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[sub][list][b][i]►►BREAKING NEWS: 26 confirmed dead in Attika, E. Ystwlsa◀◀[/b]
Terror Attack on two corridor-standard Koranvistani shipping facilities.[/i][/list]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/sub]
[i]Early this morning, in a coordinated attack, timed explosive devices were sent through two different shipping centers. Though not citing a reason, the criminal Sasanov Syndicate has claimed responsibility. 
Netizens speculate the possibility of Corridor-related retaliation.
[list][sub]"they deal, they smuggle- push corridor out, back to business baby"[/sub][/list]
Writes SkullShagger67 on WZ.kvn
[list][sub]"Were devastated," says widow, I mean, its just senseless. Tell me the mans name Ill serve justice myself.[/list][/sub][/i]
[/quote][/spoiler]

For over two weeks following the attack, the Crown was silent except for holding a national day for mourning (the 17th). The Sasanov Syndicate claimed to have paid a far-right extremist group to carry out the attacks.

The facilities in question werent severely damaged, save for some product, and were able to resume normal function within the week.

Privately, Queen Markov reached out to the leaders in The Corridor to let them know not to activate the defense mechanism. That the investigation into the attacks would be handled internally, and details would be brought to the Council by way of report.

Within days, the responsible suspects were identified, detained, and executed with the help of Sovotschegos new Artificial Intelligence model, Suza. With access to the Kingdoms CCTV network, optimized facial and pattern recognition capabilities, and layered processing functions, they were identified while trying to flee to the Massanikoan islands. This was not made public knowledge until the second of April, when the Crown broke its silence.
It was a clear, sunny day. Press were gathered by the front of the Palace, the Cabinet stood solemnly by the Queen, and the Governors (minus one, curiously enough) stood behind Them.

Queen Markov addressed those in the crowd:
[i]Terrible. It pains me to have to say this today, to be here at all. We lost 26 of our own, and though weve found the two men who carried out this attack, the search is not over.[/i]

She adjusted her stance and cleared her throat, [i]We know that theres heavy Syndicate involvement. And that it goes deeper than the Syndicate, as well. The Royal Affairs Ministry, in conjunction with local police departments and the Koranvistan military, have been investigating. Theyve compiled a conclusive report on suspects, underground networks, and will be sending it to Corridor and EDU leaders for aid in investigation and prosecution.[/i]

[b]The Syndicate Report[/b]

[i]The Royal Affairs Ministry puts forth these findings as part of an ongoing investigation into the March 15th attack:[/i]

Volkov, Igruni Mikaelovik - Deceased
[list][*]Volkov was one of two men found guilty for the March 15th attack. He was detained on his way to Massanikos and had sustained life-ending injuries while under arrest.

[*]He was carrying out orders with his conspirator on behalf of Mazlow Kabalev, known also as Squidge.[/list]

Krogoynuygyev, Nikolai Isaakov - Deceased
[list][*]Krogoynuygyev was one of two men found guilty for the March 15th attack. He was detained on his way to Massanikos and had sustained life-ending injuries while under arrest.

[*]He was carrying out orders with his conspirator on behalf of Mazlow Kabalev, known also as Squidge.

Kabalev, Mazlow Squidge - Wanted
[list][*]Squidge is the most open operative of the Kabalev Family. The Kabalevs handle the Syndicates supply chain- how the product comes in and out of Koranvistan.

[*]Known affiliates include Nikodim Chevets and Viktor Kabalev

[*]Also has contacts in [nation]Vespurias[/nation] (supplier) and abroad[/list]

Chevets, Nikodiv Asmonov - Wanted
[list][*]Head of Security for the Syndicate. Last known whereabouts were in Shamat, somewhere.[/list]

Kabalev, Viktor Yurikov - Wanted
[list][*]Head of the Kabalev Familys distribution network. Last known whereabouts: The Kingdom[/list]

[b]Divisions within the Syndicate:[/b]
The Kabalev Family - The Movers. The Kabalevs handle the Syndicates supply chain- how the product comes in and out of Koranvistan.

The Chevets Family - Highly armed security for the Syndicate operations. Generalists who train from childhood in close combat, marksmanship, etc.

The Tsorovik Family - The Smugglers, traveling from Nation to Nation with fake names and passports. They establish customer bases in untapped areas.

[spoiler= The Only Easy Day Was Yesterday
[sub]An Erene2000 Roleplay
The Battle for Kunda
Part II[/sub]]

[i]First and Fourth platoons will be moving on the far side, thats the eastern side, of Hill 005. We will have second platoon supporting your advance from the MSR, with third platoon acting as a QRF reserve for when we are ready to break through. The Air Force has already targeted multiple structures which intelligence reports identified as key enemy positions, these were buildings, defenses, you name it. They flew over and flattened the whole place early this morning, I have no doubt that many of you heard it. 

We expect the rats to have gone underground, be extremely cautious. All men should be looking for, and expecting tunnels. We have confirmed report that tunnels have been dug in Kunda itself. We dont know if they have been connected to these highlands, but its safer for us to assume that they have. It is because that we are operating under the assumption that our enemy will be beneath our feet, we will be advancing at a snails pace. Land mines, hidden launchers, hidden openings, all of these things are concerns. The rest of the brigade will be making their move with us, there is also an armored QRF force standing by to provide support. 

We will move slowly and cautiously. Our objective is to locate evidence of hidden tunnels, ensure the destruction of Target C1, that is one of the buildings I mentioned earlier that got flattened, and to secure the far eastern side of the highland. Once that is secured we can work on removing these bastards from the highlands entirely and making our move into the city. If none of you have questions, youre dismissed to brief your squad leaders.[/i]

-

The City of Kunda is the largest in Ostarevi occupied Western Toqastan. It is home to nearly 350,000 ethnic Toqa people. The city itself lays in the Great Eastern Shamat grasslands, with most of the area surrounding the city being flat and wide open. There is a group of rolling hills to the North and East of town that the locals have called The Highlands for some time. The tallest of these highlands is tall enough to have an overlooking vantage point of the City of Kunda. It is this area which the Ostarevi Armed Forces have decided to assault first.They will then establish a variety of force support elements atop the highlands in order to support operations happening within the town. The outskirts of the town lay about 7.5 miles from the highest of the highland hills. 

Leading up to the attack the 223rd Fighter Squadron of the Ostarevi Air Forces performed supported the 5th Air Attack Squadron in bombing the area and leveling many key buildings which Ostarevi Military Intelligence had identified and confirmed as enemy assets. The true level of the damage is a of yet unknown, but all buildings were confirmed to have either been leveled by the strike, or at least severely damaged. The initial attack was considered successful enough by Commanders, and a second follow up strike was not ordered. 

As the men of the 1st Separate Assault Brigade make their way towards their objective, they will be supported from high above by multiple loitering munitions systems, medium altitude long endurance unmanned reconnaissance systems, and medium altitude long endurance unmanned attack systems. Not to mention various support artillery elements, CASEVAC, and more.

[b]Debrief[/b]

How did the meeting go Cahit? asked the shah as he walked once more into the garden courtyard and sat himself easily into one of the wicker chairs, it was just him and Cahit, who sat like a blob of jelly in his motorised wheelchair, smacking down an almond biscuit.

I have my doubts that the Wuloosyans got my message, he intoned after chewing and swallowing, See these Wuloosyans, are a dedicated bunch, he continued waving around an Alaçatı kurabiyesi he had plucked from the dish that sat in the middle of the table.

I see, and you believe they intend to continue their war? asked the shah.

Without a doubt, replied Cahit between a bite of the cookie.

The shah sighed, And I thought that you would smack them out of it, he nodded sadly.

My dear shah, while I may be an ill tempered man, known for having a procilivity for assault, I do not wish to cause an international issue, Chortled Cahit, picking up a Bağdat hurma tatlısı.

So do you think we should go through with the oil threat? asked the Shah.

I advise we keep watching, and once the war powers resolution passes the citizenry, we can use those powers to our disposal, but I do not trust the wuloosyansnot one bit, Intoned Cahit as he bit into a turkish delight.

They offered some planes? asked the Shah.

Yes, a bribe no doubt, intoned Cahit.

And you accepted it? Asked the shah.

Yes, but not as a bribe my dear shah, as a necessary expenditure to increase our armed forces, he said, waggling his pointer finger while holding a baklava in his other hand.

The ethics committee might have something to say about that, intoned the shah with mild worry.

My mufti has much more to say about the ethics committee, laughed Cahit.

The shah smiled, Anyways, I wish not to keep you long, thank you for coming my friend, replied the shah, standing and patting Cahit on the arm.

Anything to get a hold of these pastries my good sir, the kitchens of Karaçe are bountiful! laughed Cahit.

[quote=pantagruel;61486331][spoiler=[nation]British Calradia[/nation]][i]Daesunite DF-21s and DF-35s were able to easily total Balionic fighters utilizing BVR technology, due to their usage of primitive dogfighting tactics, Daesunite aerial squadrons were able to strike multiple Balionic targets while facing minimal casualties with the assistance of DE-2 AWACs within the area, granting the fighters radar signatures of incoming Balionic dogfighters way outside of natural targeting zones. 

Balionic attempts to utilize asymmetric jamming warfare were also easily thwarted by the LCSG, their small speedboats proved them to be rather easy undefendable targets that could be easily neutralized out by missile strikes from airborne Mih-60r Seahawks and KUS-FC drones. 

The large movement of Balionic warships were easily detected by SBIRs and KH-11 LEOs loitering hundreds of miles above the flashzone, utilizing CEC theyd transfer live-data on the advancement of Balionic naval assets to the Hyong Yong-Chul Nimitz-class AC, which would further distribute the data to the rest of the strike group. With direct conflict with the Balionic naval armada inevitable, Daesun would seek to take a pre-emptive strike to weaken the force before it could respond articulately.

At dead of night, Dosan Ahn Chang-Ho and Virginia class submarines quietly moved towards firing range, burying themselves deep within the oceans thermal layers. Once within range, theyd initialize their launch sequence, while actively relaying information back and forth between them, the LCSG, and LEO satellites granting 24/7 recon on Balionic naval advancements. The Virginia-classes would be the vanguards of the strike, silently releasing their Mark-48 Torpedo armaments. These torpedoes were wire-guided, allowing them to be constantly updated by passive sonar detection in real time about their targets trajectories, speed, and direction, while also allowing them to distinguish between high-value targets and chaff. The first wave of torpedoes aimed to decapitate Balionic naval command, mainly their 3 active aircraft carriers. But this wasnt the end of the submarine assault, not too far behind Dosan Ahn Chango-class SSGNs would also release their armaments. Multiple cells of Tomahawk missiles screamed open atop their hulls, their VLS systems allowing them to launch deep within the ocean without the need of surfacing. Each cruise missile screamed towards the sky, before eerily cracking perpendicularly towards their targets. Guided by sophisticated DSMAC, satellite, and DE-2 data, the missiles aimed to strike their targets with near perfect precision. In the dead of night, the burning fiery aura of their exhaust is what remained visible to the naked eye. Each missile hugged the sea, working to make accurately striking them near-impossible. Their targets were mainly high-value Balionic assets such as cruisers, supply ships, and central command centers.

But the PDSF wasnt done yet, the submarine assault had only been the beginning of the high-scale attack that was to take place. From the outer rings of the LCSG defensive posture reigned the revered Sejong-class destroyers, guided missile destroyers capable of 128 vertical launches of various missile types. But their initiative in this assault remained rather controlled, rather than targeting the head of the Balionic armada theyd focus on picking off key defensive assets such as destroyers, cruisers, and radar ships. To do this, the ships would utilize a variety of missiles for the assault, mainly K-ASROC, Harpoon, SM-2 and SM-6 missiles. With prior jamming superiority in the flashzone due to the efforts of EA-18Gs and DF-21 EW variants, the Sejong-class would work in tandem with already present Growlers to synchronize an overwhelming noise jamming effort, focusing on masking their incoming missiles. Each missile attack would come in robust volleys, with older SM-2 missiles leading the advance, while their focus was to ideally strike Balionic radar nodes, theyd also be utilized to provide a second layer of chaff for the more advanced SM-6 which would be the heavy-strike in the operation, with their number gradually increasing with each volley as Balionic defenses began to get overwhelmed. K-ASROC and Harpoon missiles would also play a major role, aiming to slip past the gaze of Balionic aerial defenses and strike Balionic destroyers and cruisers, theyd minimize their potential radar signatures via sea-skimming, having the much louder SM-2 missile variants act as a virtual veil to protect them from Balionic defensive attempts. 

B-1s would zip off from airbases in Persephone and Hayan-Dal, fueled by KC-135 tankers as they headed towards the strike zone. Once the Balionic armada was within striking distance, the B-1s would release waves of LRASM missiles totalling over 100. These missiles aimed to strike while Balionic defenses were being stressed by the earlier salvo, overlapping with the targets of missile variants in case they were to fail. 

Atop the deck of the Admiral Hyong Yong-Chul AC, squadrons of DF-35Cs screamed off the runway, 24 in total. Due to their RAM coating and significantly miniscule radar cross-section, the DF-35Cs were able covertly slip within strike range of the already jammed Balionic fleet. Each carrying 2 LRASMs. Their objective wasnt to provide another layer of saturation against the Balionic defenses, but to act as the killing blow to high-value assets. In total, 48 LRASMs screeched towards their targets, mainly remaining Balionic radar ships, cruisers, and carriers. Their integrated IR evasion and naturalized sea-skimming capabilities allowed them to become formidable targets becoming near-invisible to most detection systems besides their bright orange flare illuminating the night.

Daesun would further reinforce the skies with squadrons of DF-2 Multirole fighters, due to their lack of stealth technology the DF-2s opted to stay within the defenses of the LCSG. Utilizing hit and block tactics, the DF-2s would conduct naval strikes on Balionic stragglers with ASM-2 missiles and then retreat to the defenses of the LCSG, allowing for the force to take both offensive and defensive postures.

In the final phases of the night operation, P-8 Poseidons and Mih-60rs would intensify ASW operations within the defensive range of the LCSG. The Poseidons sonobuoys allowed for them to pick up on the loud humming of the diesel powered submarines engines, granting them the ability to effectively trace and locate any remaining Balionic submarine. Which would be quickly met by both the Seahawk and Poseidons Mk-54 ASW torpedoes. 

With the pre-emptive strike operation executed, Daesunite marines aboard the LCSG would prepare final training operations before the eventual amphibious landing on Empire Island. The amphibious force now totalled over 120,000, with marines stationed in Persephone and Hayan-Dal enroute to the LCSG escorted by Sejong-class destroyers.[/i]
